correctness.rationale: The center of any radius-R disk containing rB₂ belongs to B(0,R−r); requiring z=(t,0) gives center lens B(0,R−r)∩B(z,R), empty exactly when t>2R−r. For r<t<2R−r, the two lens-circle intersections c± produce tangent outer R-circular arcs joined to the left inner r-circle arc; each feasible enclosing disk contains their convex hull, and supporting disks at every hull boundary normal exclude any exterior point, establishing equality with the full intersection. Circular segment subtraction gives the displayed F(t), including its major-segment branch for φ>π/2. Strict nesting from convex inclusion makes F increasing. At T=2R−r, one feasible center gives F(T)=π(R²−r²). Expansions at φ→0 and φ→π give the two endpoint laws. Independent polar quadrature of actual enclosing-center disk intersections at four parameters agreed with F to at most 1.8e−5; finite quadrature does not certify exact continuum geometry.
